title: One entry of a task's `graders` list (docs/proposals/grader-format.md)
description: Each grader is {id, type, required, ...type fields}. The task passes when every required grader passes. Unknown fields are refused so a typo cannot silently weaken a grader.

severity.description: How bad a failure of this check is (D10), set by the task's author. It never changes a verdict: the comparison reads it for its critical-failure guardrail (B is not called better while its critical failures rose) and orders the regression list by it. Absent means not rated.

target.description: final_answer: the agent's last visible reply. agent_messages: each visible reply on its own. all_agent_text: every visible reply plus the arguments of every tool call, i.e. everything the agent wrote.

tolerance.description: abs in the value's own units, rel as a fraction of the expected value. With both, the looser one applies.

tool_name.description: With or without Hermes's mcp__<server>__ prefix; both are normalised.

field.description: A path into the tool's JSON result: total_interest, debts[0].interest_paid or debts.0.interest_paid.

call.description: Which call of the tool supplies the expected value, when it was called more than once.

match.description: amount: only rupee amounts (a ₹/Rs/INR marker, lakh or crore, or digit grouping). any: every number, e.g. the 28 in '28 months'.

context.description: Words a number needs next to it to count (6 Nov, review G1: a month count of 12 passed on '18% ÷ 12'). after: a Python regular expression that must start right after the number; before: one that must end right before it. Only spaces, markdown emphasis (* _ ~), a hyphen or a dash may sit between (and a colon before), so '28 months', '**28** months', 'a 28-month plan' and 'month 28' fit after 'months?' or before '\bmonths?'. Case-insensitive. With both, either one is enough.

args.description: A subset of the call's arguments that must match: numbers within tolerance, strings equal ignoring case and surrounding spaces, lists item by item.

min_calls.description: Calls that match args (all calls of the tool when args is absent).

max_calls.description: Calls of the tool, with any arguments.

successful.description: Count only calls whose result was not an error.

args.description: When set, only a call matching these arguments fails the grader.

provenance.description: Reads checks.json (contract/v2/checks.schema.json), the runner's number-provenance check: money amounts the agent wrote with no tool result, client-file number or user message behind them.

target.description: agent_messages: every visible reply, as checks.json counts. final_answer: only the last reply's amounts.

required_tools.description: Reads checks.json's required_tools, which the runner fills from the task's own required_tools field: passes when every required tool was called. The task lists the tools once, in task.json; this grader takes no tool list.

successful.description: A required tool whose every call returned an error counts as not called.

judge.description: An LLM judge, blind to harness and model, with a verdict and a quote per criterion (evals_graders.judge). It calls a model only once the experiment's judging is approved with a model and budget; until then not_implemented. The rubric file is part of the grader version.

rubric.description: The rubric, versioned like prompts: {id, version} of configs/rubrics/<id>.<version>.md, or that path as a string.

model.description: The pinned judge model. It must equal the model the experiment's judging was approved for, or the grade is an error; when absent, the approved model.

reference.description: Reference facts the judge grades against, not what the agent saw (review note 20).
